methods.description: Checks that the instance responds
Instance summary: file, lines, annotations, step, terminal size

by.description:
Who put it there last: the presenter (`f`, then the cursor or the
selection moves it) or an agent (`pointer.set`).

to.description: Last pointed line (`line` itself for a single line).

PointerBy.description: Who moved the live pointer last (t-030).

auto_advance_ms.description: `auto_advance_ms` of the current step, when it has one.

autosave.description:
Whether every change is written to the sidecar as it happens
(`--no-save`, `:autosave off` and a `scene.put` of another document
turn it off; `:w` saves explicitly either way).

build.description: Git commit the instance was built from (`unknown` outside a checkout).

file.description:
The file shown: the source file, or the one a `code.link` move
left up at the current step (t-105).

first_line.description:
First and last line of the shown code (the window of a `code.link`
with `lines`, the whole file otherwise).

loop.description: The document loops: past the last step comes step 0.

margin.description: Right-margin cap in cells (`:margin N`, document field); absent = dynamic.

numbers.description: Whether the line-number gutter is shown (`:numbers`, document field).

pointer.description:
The live pointer (t-030): the lines the presenter (`f`) or an agent
(`pointer.set`) is pointing at on the screen right now, or `null`.
Never saved nor exported. Always present.

redact_alerts.description:
The loud redact notices on the presenter's screen, oldest first
(t-156): a redact widened or dropped by a reload, a paste or a move
(t-117, t-140, t-157) and a move retargeted by another (t-157), the
same rows the TUI draws above its bar (t-135). Ids, lines and
visible text only, never text under a mask. A later reload does not
clear them; the presenter's next key does (they were seen). Always
present, `[]` when nothing is pending.

step_id.description:
The `id` and `title` of the current step, when `steps` names it
(t-099); `step_label` is what the status line shows
(`step 3/7 · Shared borrow`).

supervised.description: Supervised mode: mutations wait for the presenter's approval.

view.description:
The `code.link` view shown, as `file` or `file:A-B`; absent on the
main file.

warnings.description:
Human-readable warnings about the viewport (small terminal, clipped
code) and the document (a `steps` entry past the last step).

methods.description: This list
JSON Schema of every method (params and result) and of the request/response lines

MethodSchema.description: One method of the local API with the schema of its params and result.

result.description: The whole API contract, as `api.schema` and `tiza schema api` return it.

request.description: Shape of every request and response line.

result.title: ApiSchema

methods.description: Code shown at the current step with line numbers (text), and the file/window it comes from
Full document with annotations and current step (code embedded)

Anchor.description: A point in the code: absolute line (1-based) and grapheme (0-based).

oneOf.description: Highlights a text range.

Highlight with meaning. `kind` names a built-in kind (`read`, `warn`, `move`…),
an alias, or a reusable style from `Document::styles`; `style` overrides any
field inline for this one annotation.
Box around a range of lines.
Arrow from one point of the code to another.
Text note anchored to a line.

Bordered multi-line text block explaining a range of lines. Laid out as a
block (reserving its rows), not as a per-line label, so a paragraph does
not push every other label down.

Masks a span of code (a token, a password, a URL with credentials):
on every surface the span shows as eight `•` plus the last `keep`
characters, never the real text or its length (t-117). Active from
step 0 whatever its `step`, unless `Document::redact_from_step`.
Only the columns are stored: never the text under them.

keep.description: Characters left visible at the end of the span (0..=8).

pin.description:
On a document with moves, which code the span's columns refer to
(t-154), set by Tiza when it pins the redact: `0` the untouched
file, `N` the code right after move #N (1-based), the move that
wrote its line. Absent: the code at the end of the annotation's
`step` (ADR 0007 §3d; `step: 0` is the untouched file). Moves
added or deleted later keep it on that same text.

widened.description:
Set by a reload or paste that could not follow the redact's text
(fail-closed, t-117): the mask was widened to the rest of its
line, or to whole lines, and keeps no tail. Cleared when the
presenter marks the value again (a new redact over it).

oneOf.description:
Directs attention: while active (from `step` to `until`, or only at
`step`), dims the code outside `lines` and the annotations outside `ids`.
With only `ids`, the focused code is that of those annotations.

color.description:
Color chosen by the presenter: a palette name (`blue`, `verde`…) or `#rrggbb`.
Without a color, arrows rotate through a palette and the rest use the theme color.

file.description:
The file (view) the annotation belongs to, as a `code.link` names it
(t-105). Absent: the document's main file. Filled in from the view
shown at the annotation's step when it is added without one. Lines
are always real file line numbers; the annotation is drawn only
while its file is shown and its lines fall inside the window.

id.description: Short, stable public id (`a1`, `a2`…), chosen by the client or assigned.

markers.description:
Range shapes (box, callout, spotlight) created from two text markers
(`find_start` / `find_end`, t-097): kept so the range can be
re-resolved after the code changes (t-098). Lines stay the truth.

step.description:
Step at which it appears (1-based). A redact may say 0 on a document
with moves: it masks from step 0 anyway, and its step only says which
code its columns refer to (0: the untouched file, t-140).

anyOf.description: Copy of the code inside the document: portable, but frozen.

Reference to an existing file. `file` may be absolute or relative to the
`.tiza` directory; `lines` is an optional range `"12-48"` or `"7"`.

CodeSource.description: Where the code of a `.tiza` comes from.

CursorAt.description: `cursor`: a line (real file line number) and an optional grapheme column.

code.description:
How the code is stored in the file: embedded (array of lines) or a
reference to a file (`{"file": "src/main.rs", "lines": "12-48"}`).

loop.description: `n` (and an `auto_advance_ms`) past the last step goes back to step 0.

margin.description:
Cap on the right margin, in cells (t-113): long notes wrap at it
instead of spreading across a wide terminal. `None`: dynamic.

moves.description:
Code changes between steps (ADR 0007): applied when the presenter
reaches `at_step`, reverted when going back. The embedded `code` is
always the step-0 code.

numbers.description:
Line-number gutter (t-112). Off, the code starts at the left edge
(lanes and boxes move with it); the TUI, `render` and the agents'
renders all follow it. `render --no-numbers` / `--numbers` override
it for one export.

padding.description: Blank cells around the drawing: `[vertical, horizontal]`. Saved so each take looks the same.

redact_from_step.description:
Redact masks follow their annotation's `step` instead of being active
from step 0 (off by default: a secret is never shown at an earlier step).

step.description:
Current presentation step. 0 = code only, no annotations;
annotations live at steps ≥ 1.

steps.description:
Named steps (ADR 0007 §4, t-099): a title, an id for `step.goto` and
an optional `auto_advance_ms`, bound to a step by its explicit
`step` number (never by the position in the list, so moving an
annotation to another step shifts nothing). Sparse; saved sorted by
`step`. Automation for recordings and booth loops, not speaker tools.

styles.description: Reusable mark styles defined by the author, referenced by name in `kind`.

theme_overrides.description:
Per-token theme overrides (t-119), the same keys as the `[theme]`
table of `~/.config/tiza/config.toml`; they apply on top of the
config file's and under `:theme`.

views.description:
Code of the files `code.link` moves name, frozen inside the document
by `:embed` (one entry per file, keyed as the move names it; the
window stays in the move). A file absent here is read from disk next
to the `.tiza` when the document loads.

Emphasis.description: How a highlighted or marked span is drawn (t-096).

oneOf.description: Background tint (the default).
A row under the line with ▔ under the span.
⌈ ⌉ in the cells beside the span (a glued side goes to the row below).
A long stroke through every character.

Head.description: What is drawn at an end of a line.

Heads.description: Heads at both ends. Default: nothing at the start, `▶` at the end.

Link.description:
`code.link`: `file` is the path as `code.file` would name it (relative to
the `.tiza` directory); `lines` is only a window (`"7-30"` or `"7"`) that
crops what is shown — annotations keep real file line numbers and the
same file with another window is the same view.

MarkStyle.description:
Semantic marks for explaining Rust (each with a fixed color, glyph and legend).
Visual style of a mark: a glyph, a short legend and a color name. Styles come
from three places, in priority order: an inline `style` on the annotation, the
document's reusable `styles` map, and the built-in kinds (see [`BUILTIN_KINDS`]).

glyph.description: One or two cells wide (box-drawing, arrows, emoji…). Measured, never assumed.

legend.description: Text shown after the glyph; the annotation's `label` is appended after `: `.

oneOf.description: Insert, replace or delete whole lines of the file shown at the step.

Show another file (or the main file again), optionally cropped to a
window of lines. Each file is a view with its own annotations.
Put the cursor on a line (and column) of the shown file.
Select a span of the shown file, from one point to another.

Pause for `ms` before the step's annotations appear (TUI and
recordings; a still render ignores it).

at_step.description: Step at which it runs (going forward) and is reverted (going back). `>= 1`.

rebind.description:
Where annotations the patch replaces or deletes go afterwards, by id,
with the same fields as `annotation.update`'s `move`: `{"at": {"find":
"…", "occurrence": N}}` or `{"at": {"line": N, "col": C}}` for
highlights, marks and notes; `{"from": {…}, "to": {…}}` for arrows;
`{"from_line": A, "to_line": B}` for boxes, callouts and spotlights.
Resolved against the code after the patch. A spec with none of those
keys (or an unknown one) is a load-time error.

MoveSpec.description:
Partial re-anchoring of an existing annotation. Which fields apply depends
on the shape: `at` for highlights, marks and notes; `from`/`to` for arrows;
`from_line`/`to_line` for boxes, callouts, spotlights and notes. A field
that does not apply to the annotation's type is an `invalid_argument`
error, never silently ignored; so is an unknown key (`{"find": …}`
without `at` is rejected, not ignored).

auto_advance_ms.description:
Go to the next step on its own this many milliseconds after the step
is ready (its typing finished and its `wait` moves elapsed). The
native GIF/MP4 hold the step's frame this long instead of `--interval`.

id.description:
What `step.goto {id}`, MCP `goto_step` and `tiza goto ID` jump to.
Unique, no blanks, and not all digits (a number means a step number).

step.description:
The step this entry names (0 = the code alone). Explicit, so
reordering the list or moving annotations never rebinds it.

title.description: Shown on the status line (`step 3/7 · Shared borrow`) and in `status`.

anyOf.description:
`#rrggbb`, `#rgb`, `rgb(r, g, b)`, a palette or ANSI name, or
`reset` (the terminal's default colour; exports fall back).
Overrides that apply only when this base theme is active.

OverrideValue.description:
One value of a `[theme]` table: a colour, or the `dark` / `light`
subtable that applies on top when that base theme is active.

after.description: `insert`: text of the line the content goes after / before (exactly one line matches).

content.description: New lines (`insert`, `replace`); `\n` separates lines, a trailing `\n` is ignored.

find.description: `replace`/`delete`: text of the one line to change.

find_start.description: `replace`/`delete`: the range from the line of `find_start` to the line of `find_end`.

occurrence.description:
Which match of `find` / `after` / `before` / `find_start` to use when
the text appears more than once: 1-based, counted in reading order
over the whole code as it is at this step (ADR 0007 §2). Without it,
more than one match is an error.

position.description:
`insert`: the line the content goes before (`last + 1` appends).
`replace`/`delete`: the line range (`"7"` or `"7-9"`).

speed_ms.description: Milliseconds per line (`typing: line`, default 120) or per character (`char`, default 25).

oneOf.description: In the right margin, aligned with `from_line` (default).
As its own rows between `to_line` and the next code line.
Margin when the terminal has room, below otherwise.

RangeMarkers.description:
Two texts that delimit a line range: the first occurrence of `start`
anywhere, then the first occurrence of `end` at or after it.

Route.description: Corner shape of a routed line: `╭╰` (rounded, the cell-grid "curve") or `┌└` (sharp).

SelectSpec.description:
`select`: two points of the shown file, each a `find` (exactly one match
at that step, or with `occurrence`) or a `line`/`col`. With `find`, the
selection starts at the start of `from`'s text and ends at the end of
`to`'s text.

first_line.description: Number of the first displayed line (allows opening `main.rs:12-48`).

path.description: Path of the original file, if there was one.

TextSpan.description: A range within ONE line, in graphemes, exclusive end.

oneOf.description:
The host terminal's own palette (t-119): default background and
foreground, roles on the 16 ANSI colours, syntax on the terminal's
colours. Only meaningful in the TUI; exports fall back to dark/light.

ThemeOverrides.description:
The `[theme]` table of `~/.config/tiza/config.toml`, a `--theme-file`,
or a document's `theme_overrides`: Tiza's roles by name (`bg`, `fg`,
`muted`, `dimmed`, `accent`, `rail`, `box_line`, `box_bg`, `arrow`,
`note`, `highlight_bg`, `status_bg`, `status_fg`, `cmd_bg`, `error`),
the named annotation palette (`orange`, `blue`, `green`, `purple`,
`pink`, `cyan`, `yellow`, `red`, `gray`), and `dark` / `light`
subtables with the same keys.

Where to anchor something: explicit coordinates or a text search.
An agent rarely knows the exact column; `find` is more robust.

end.description: With `line` and `col`: end of the span (exclusive). Without it the span runs to the end of the line.

find.description: Text to search for in the code; with `line`, that line is searched first.

result.description:

revision of [`Mutated`], plus where the annotation stands against the
view at the moment the change is applied. In supervised mode that is
when the presenter accepts the proposal, so `shown_step` may differ from
the step the agent saw when it asked; the view can move again right
after, so read it as a snapshot, not as a promise.

CodeSource.description: Where the code of a `.tiza` comes from.

CursorAt.description: `cursor`: a line (real file line number) and an optional grapheme column.

code.description:
How the code is stored in the file: embedded (array of lines) or a
reference to a file (`{"file": "src/main.rs", "lines": "12-48"}`).

loop.description: `n` (and an `auto_advance_ms`) past the last step goes back to step 0.

margin.description:
Cap on the right margin, in cells (t-113): long notes wrap at it
instead of spreading across a wide terminal. `None`: dynamic.

moves.description:
Code changes between steps (ADR 0007): applied when the presenter
reaches `at_step`, reverted when going back. The embedded `code` is
always the step-0 code.

numbers.description:
Line-number gutter (t-112). Off, the code starts at the left edge
(lanes and boxes move with it); the TUI, `render` and the agents'
renders all follow it. `render --no-numbers` / `--numbers` override
it for one export.

padding.description: Blank cells around the drawing: `[vertical, horizontal]`. Saved so each take looks the same.

redact_from_step.description:
Redact masks follow their annotation's `step` instead of being active
from step 0 (off by default: a secret is never shown at an earlier step).

step.description:
Current presentation step. 0 = code only, no annotations;
annotations live at steps ≥ 1.

steps.description:
Named steps (ADR 0007 §4, t-099): a title, an id for `step.goto` and
an optional `auto_advance_ms`, bound to a step by its explicit
`step` number (never by the position in the list, so moving an
annotation to another step shifts nothing). Sparse; saved sorted by
`step`. Automation for recordings and booth loops, not speaker tools.

styles.description: Reusable mark styles defined by the author, referenced by name in `kind`.

theme_overrides.description:
Per-token theme overrides (t-119), the same keys as the `[theme]`
table of `~/.config/tiza/config.toml`; they apply on top of the
config file's and under `:theme`.

views.description:
Code of the files `code.link` moves name, frozen inside the document
by `:embed` (one entry per file, keyed as the move names it; the
window stays in the move). A file absent here is read from disk next
to the `.tiza` when the document loads.

Emphasis.description: How a highlighted or marked span is drawn (t-096).

oneOf.description: Background tint (the default).
A row under the line with ▔ under the span.
⌈ ⌉ in the cells beside the span (a glued side goes to the row below).
A long stroke through every character.

Head.description: What is drawn at an end of a line.

Heads.description: Heads at both ends. Default: nothing at the start, `▶` at the end.

Link.description:
`code.link`: `file` is the path as `code.file` would name it (relative to
the `.tiza` directory); `lines` is only a window (`"7-30"` or `"7"`) that
crops what is shown — annotations keep real file line numbers and the
same file with another window is the same view.

MarkStyle.description:
Semantic marks for explaining Rust (each with a fixed color, glyph and legend).
Visual style of a mark: a glyph, a short legend and a color name. Styles come
from three places, in priority order: an inline `style` on the annotation, the
document's reusable `styles` map, and the built-in kinds (see [`BUILTIN_KINDS`]).

glyph.description: One or two cells wide (box-drawing, arrows, emoji…). Measured, never assumed.

legend.description: Text shown after the glyph; the annotation's `label` is appended after `: `.

oneOf.description: Insert, replace or delete whole lines of the file shown at the step.

Show another file (or the main file again), optionally cropped to a
window of lines. Each file is a view with its own annotations.
Put the cursor on a line (and column) of the shown file.
Select a span of the shown file, from one point to another.

Pause for `ms` before the step's annotations appear (TUI and
recordings; a still render ignores it).

at_step.description: Step at which it runs (going forward) and is reverted (going back). `>= 1`.

rebind.description:
Where annotations the patch replaces or deletes go afterwards, by id,
with the same fields as `annotation.update`'s `move`: `{"at": {"find":
"…", "occurrence": N}}` or `{"at": {"line": N, "col": C}}` for
highlights, marks and notes; `{"from": {…}, "to": {…}}` for arrows;
`{"from_line": A, "to_line": B}` for boxes, callouts and spotlights.
Resolved against the code after the patch. A spec with none of those
keys (or an unknown one) is a load-time error.

MoveSpec.description:
Partial re-anchoring of an existing annotation. Which fields apply depends
on the shape: `at` for highlights, marks and notes; `from`/`to` for arrows;
`from_line`/`to_line` for boxes, callouts, spotlights and notes. A field
that does not apply to the annotation's type is an `invalid_argument`
error, never silently ignored; so is an unknown key (`{"find": …}`
without `at` is rejected, not ignored).

auto_advance_ms.description:
Go to the next step on its own this many milliseconds after the step
is ready (its typing finished and its `wait` moves elapsed). The
native GIF/MP4 hold the step's frame this long instead of `--interval`.

id.description:
What `step.goto {id}`, MCP `goto_step` and `tiza goto ID` jump to.
Unique, no blanks, and not all digits (a number means a step number).

step.description:
The step this entry names (0 = the code alone). Explicit, so
reordering the list or moving annotations never rebinds it.

title.description: Shown on the status line (`step 3/7 · Shared borrow`) and in `status`.

anyOf.description:
`#rrggbb`, `#rgb`, `rgb(r, g, b)`, a palette or ANSI name, or
`reset` (the terminal's default colour; exports fall back).
Overrides that apply only when this base theme is active.

OverrideValue.description:
One value of a `[theme]` table: a colour, or the `dark` / `light`
subtable that applies on top when that base theme is active.

after.description: `insert`: text of the line the content goes after / before (exactly one line matches).

content.description: New lines (`insert`, `replace`); `\n` separates lines, a trailing `\n` is ignored.

find.description: `replace`/`delete`: text of the one line to change.

find_start.description: `replace`/`delete`: the range from the line of `find_start` to the line of `find_end`.

occurrence.description:
Which match of `find` / `after` / `before` / `find_start` to use when
the text appears more than once: 1-based, counted in reading order
over the whole code as it is at this step (ADR 0007 §2). Without it,
more than one match is an error.

position.description:
`insert`: the line the content goes before (`last + 1` appends).
`replace`/`delete`: the line range (`"7"` or `"7-9"`).

speed_ms.description: Milliseconds per line (`typing: line`, default 120) or per character (`char`, default 25).

oneOf.description: In the right margin, aligned with `from_line` (default).

Margin when the terminal has room, below otherwise.

RangeMarkers.description:

anywhere, then the first occurrence of `end` at or after it.

Route.description: Corner shape of a routed line: `╭╰` (rounded, the cell-grid "curve") or `┌└` (sharp).

SelectSpec.description:

at that step, or with `occurrence`) or a `line`/`col`. With `find`, the
selection starts at the start of `from`'s text and ends at the end of
`to`'s text.

first_line.description: Number of the first displayed line (allows opening `main.rs:12-48`).

path.description: Path of the original file, if there was one.

TextSpan.description: A range within ONE line, in graphemes, exclusive end.

oneOf.description:

foreground, roles on the 16 ANSI colours, syntax on the terminal's
colours. Only meaningful in the TUI; exports fall back to dark/light.

`muted`, `dimmed`, `accent`, `rail`, `box_line`, `box_bg`, `arrow`,
`note`, `highlight_bg`, `status_bg`, `status_fg`, `cmd_bg`, `error`),
the named annotation palette (`orange`, `blue`, `green`, `purple`,
`pink`, `cyan`, `yellow`, `red`, `gray`), and `dark` / `light`
subtables with the same keys.

Where to anchor something: explicit coordinates or a text search.
An agent rarely knows the exact column; `find` is more robust.

end.description: With `line` and `col`: end of the span (exclusive). Without it the span runs to the end of the line.

find.description: Text to search for in the code; with `line`, that line is searched first.
